nodes.body: Is enforcement of this in a later commit?

I haven't added any enforcement; and I don't know why we would actually need enforcement. This just documents that "expect to be broken if you try to apply some non-Kubernetes-conformant behavior for a condition with a type of domain k8s.io, as Kubernetes will apply its own semantics to conditions with these type strings".

We in fact want people to author conditions with type e.g. `k8s.io/cel` type, so we can evaluate things in-tree.
Is this necessary if all code calling this function is feature gated?

All callers within the kube-apiserver are feature-gated, but not necessarily arbitrary library users, hence I added this to make sure no conditional decisions flow through any system when the feature gate is off. This matters, as enforcement in admission is only on when the feature gate is, so I don't want even a theoretical scenario when someone would not enable the feature (so there's no enforcement), but somehow would manage to construct a conditional decision, and pass it through their custom API server (when using `k8s.io/apiserver` the library)

This misses unconditional allow/noopinion/deny decisions nested down within further union subdecisions, right?

Yes, and that is kind of intentional for now. In the last meeting we said that in the cases where we fold

1. ConditionsMap [Allow/NoOpinion]
1. NoOpinion (reason 123)
1. Allow (reason 456)

to Allow, we only pick the last decisions' reason 456.

For the Allow/Deny case, we know (as per the comment also) that the Allow/Deny decision is the last one, if it exists, as we stopped collecting anything else afterwards. Today in the union authorizer we return only the reason and error from the first authorizer that returned Allow/Deny, so this basically mirrors that logic, ignoring any conditional decisions before that might or might not have come to the same conclusion. To make this explicit, we could return a reason like: `foo: could return any of [Allow NoOpinion], bar: allow policy "lucas-read-pods" matched`, where `foo` returned a `ConditionsMap` and `bar` unconditional `Allow`. Is that a good compromise?

For the all-NoOpinion case (which exists already today), this is similar: all sub-NoOpinion's reasons and errors are collected.
